name: Tourism Holdings Limited
sector: Travel & Leisure / RV Rental, Manufacturing and Tourism Experiences
overview: Tourism Holdings Limited (thl) is the world's largest commercial recreational vehicle (RV) rental operator, running a vertically integrated build/rent/sell model across New Zealand, Australia, and North America (USA and Canada), having exited the UK and Ireland market via divestment completed 31 March 2026. The group manufactures RVs through its Action Manufacturing business (now consolidated in Hamilton, New Zealand), rents them under a portfolio of global brands (maui, Britz, Mighty, Apollo, Cheapa, Road Bear, El Monte RV, Just Go), sells ex-fleet and new vehicles through owned dealerships, and operates New Zealand tourism attractions (Kiwi Experience, Discover Waitomo Glowworm Caves). Dual-listed on the NZX and ASX under 'THL', it is currently the subject of two competing, non-binding, conditional takeover approaches (both in active due diligence as of the FY2026 result) while executing a self-styled 'Growth Roadmap' targeting NZ$100 million of annualised NPAT within three to four years.

business_model.summary: thl generates profit at each stage of the RV's lifecycle: it builds or buys vehicles (Action Manufacturing in New Zealand, now consolidated post the December 2025 Brisbane closure), rents them to domestic and international tourists across four geographic segments, and then sells the ex-fleet vehicle through owned retail dealerships (new and used) once it has cycled through the rental fleet — a strategy designed to capture margin on build, rent and sell rather than relying on any single stage. Rental (sale of services) revenue is the core, highest-margin, most consistent earnings engine and grew 11% to $517.5m in FY2026, and is management's stated priority and 'the engine' of the business; RV sales (sale of goods) revenue fell 22% to $335.4m in FY2026 and remains a volatile, cyclical swing factor in group profitability, with industry-wide conditions described as the most difficult in years. A small but strategically important Tourism segment (Kiwi Experience guided coach tours, Waitomo Glowworm Caves) delivers stable, very high-return earnings in New Zealand (FY2026 ROFE 182%, the highest in the group). Revenue is transactional (day-rate rentals, vehicle sale transactions) rather than recurring/subscription in nature, though rental forward-booking visibility of several months provides meaningful revenue predictability — management now regularly discloses forward booking intake as a leading indicator. The customer base is predominantly B2C: international and domestic leisure travellers for rentals and tourism experiences, and retail consumers (including many first-time and 'lifetime RV owner' buyers) for vehicle sales, with no reliance on any single external customer for 10% or more of group revenue.

revenue_streams.name: Australia Rentals, Sales & Manufacturing
revenue_streams.trend: rentals up 20% (fleet +10%, RevPARV +3%); retail sales down 31% on rationalisation of two closed dealerships; underlying EBIT up 32%

revenue_streams.name: North America Rentals & Sales (USA + Canada)
revenue_streams.trend: rentals flat (+1%) despite weak USA demand, Canada tracking record season; sales down 32%; underlying EBIT swung to +$5.0m from +$1.5m on 'one fleet' synergies

revenue_streams.name: New Zealand Rentals & Sales
revenue_streams.trend: rentals up 17%, EBIT up 9% to $52.7m, ROFE 13.3% (highest of the three geographic rental segments); vehicle sales volumes resilient

revenue_streams.name: Action Manufacturing (New Zealand)
revenue_streams.trend: now consolidates all Australasian production after Brisbane closure (Dec 2025); third-party manufacturing EBIT up 55%; substantially intercompany, eliminates at group level

revenue_streams.name: Tourism (Kiwi Experience, Waitomo Glowworm Caves)
revenue_streams.trend: stable, EBIT flat at $13.8m; highest ROFE in the group (182%); Waitomo cave lease expires 2027, future under discussion

revenue_streams.name: United Kingdom & Ireland Rentals & Sales
revenue_streams.trend: divested 31 March 2026 to Indie Campers for ~$57m proceeds including ~$8m of goodwill; now presented as a discontinued operation under NZ IFRS 5 for FY2026, with FY2025 comparatives restated to exclude it

business_model.customer_type: B2C — domestic and international leisure travellers (rentals, tourism attractions) and retail consumers purchasing new/ex-fleet RVs and campervans (including a large 'lifetime RV owner' base); no B2B/enterprise customer concentration
business_model.geographic_mix: FY2026 continuing-operations segment revenue: Australia ~36% (rentals, sales & manufacturing), North America ~24% (USA + Canada), New Zealand ~23% (rentals/sales) plus Action Manufacturing ~20% (mostly intercompany, physically NZ-based), Tourism ~5%. UK & Ireland (formerly ~5% of group revenue) fully divested 31 March 2026. Geographic mix has structurally shifted toward the Southern Hemisphere (NZ/Australia now the clear majority of continuing revenue and earnings)
business_model.note: Segment percentages now derived from the FY2026 FULL-YEAR segment disclosure in the FY2026 Annual Results Presentation (12 months to 30 June 2026, continuing operations), replacing the prior H1-FY2026-only estimate. Manufacturing revenue is substantially intercompany (sold into NZ/Australia rental and retail segments) and eliminates at group level, so external group revenue is somewhat lower-weighted toward manufacturing than the raw segment figures suggest. Total consolidated FY2026 revenue was $885.3m (continuing operations $852.9m plus discontinued UK/Ireland operations $32.4m, the latter including intercompany revenue eliminated at group level); on a divisional-table basis excluding intercompany the group total was $880.2m.

main_competitors: Cruise America (largest independent RV rental competitor in the USA)
El Monte RV and Road Bear RV (thl's own North American brands, but the segment also faces independent regional operators)
McRent, Indie Campers (acquirer of thl's UK & Ireland business), Roadsurfer, Yescapa, Escape Campervans, JUCY Rentals, Spaceships, Bunk Campers (Europe/Australasia RV rental operators)
Peer-to-peer RV/campervan marketplaces (Outdoorsy, RVshare) offering an asset-light alternative to fleet ownership

Independent regional RV dealers and manufacturers in each domestic retail sales market (Australia, NZ, North America); THOR Industries and Camping World are the large listed US peers whose guidance is a read-through on industry conditions
Other leisure/travel operators competing for the broader discretionary tourism and free-independent-travel wallet
competitive_position.market_position: thl describes itself as the world's largest commercial RV rental fleet operator, with a closing FY2026 fleet of 8,587 vehicles (up 10% year-on-year), and holds the largest single-company RV rental fleet in Australasia and a top-tier position in North America. The global RV/campervan rental market itself is highly fragmented, estimated at roughly US$1.2-2.9bn depending on definition, growing mid-single digits; thl's scale advantage is most pronounced in Australasia, where full vertical integration (manufacture-rent-sell) is a genuine structural differentiator versus smaller, rental-only or sales-only competitors. Following the UK & Ireland exit and Brisbane manufacturing closure, thl's footprint is now more concentrated (NZ, Australia, USA, Canada) and more fully integrated in Australasia.

moat_factors.description: thl captures margin at each stage of a vehicle's life — Action Manufacturing (now the sole Australasian production base after Brisbane's closure) feeds cheaper fleet builds, in-house design optimises vehicles for rental durability and resale value, and owned retail dealerships extract superior residual value versus wholesaling ex-fleet units to third parties. This is strongest in Australasia, where thl is fully integrated; North America relies more on third-party sourcing

A global multi-brand fleet of 8,500+ vehicles requires substantial capital that smaller, regional operators struggle to match, and gives thl negotiating leverage with OEM chassis suppliers and access to more favourable fleet financing terms — a genuine, if not insurmountable, barrier to a new entrant replicating thl's scale

Brands spanning Signature/premium (maui) through Flagship, Adventure and Value tiers (Britz, Mighty, Apollo, Cheapa, Road Bear, El Monte RV, Just Go) let thl address multiple price points and traveller segments from a shared fleet and back-office infrastructure, capturing demand thl would otherwise cede to lower-cost competitors

A completed single global platform migration (Motek fleet management, Microsoft Dynamics 365) and the CamperMate travel app give thl operational efficiency and demand-generation advantages, plus several months of forward-booking revenue visibility management now discloses in detail as a leading indicator (e.g. Canada forward bookings up ~25-30% at various points in FY2026, before the Middle East conflict disruption)

Waitomo Glowworm Caves and Kiwi Experience are difficult-to-replicate, geographically unique or first-mover assets in the domestic NZ tourism market, delivering the group's highest returns on capital (182% ROFE in FY2026), though the Waitomo cave lease expires in 2027 and its future is under discussion with stakeholders

weaknesses: RV sales (the 'Sell' segment) is a highly cyclical, low-differentiation business exposed to consumer discretionary spending, interest rates and used-vehicle residual values; ex-fleet sales volumes fell 25% and retail RV sales volumes fell 27% in FY2026, and industry participants (THOR, Camping World) have cut 2026 forecasts further during the year
Fragmented competitive set with low switching costs for renters (price/brand comparison is easy online) and limited pricing power versus a genuinely oligopolistic or network-effect business

USA market exposure to tariffs (on RV chassis/components) and weak inbound international tourism demand has been a persistent drag; North America ROFE was still only 0.5% in FY2026 (improved from negative in FY2025) and management describes the USA as 'our largest opportunity for improvement' and 'not yet where we need to be'

Historically low Return on Funds Employed (ROFE) relative to the group's own 15% target (8.7% in FY2026, up from 7.6% in FY2025) indicates the capital-intensive fleet has not been generating adequate returns through the down-cycle, with Australia (6.8%) and North America (0.5%) well below target
Geographic and currency complexity (NZD, AUD, USD, CAD) adds translation risk and operational complexity that smaller, single-market competitors do not face

Two live, non-binding takeover approaches create an overhang and distraction risk: management has explicitly disclosed incurring transaction costs relating to the approaches, and a collapse of both processes could trigger a sharp de-rating back toward standalone fundamental value

growth_drivers: Growth Roadmap targeting NZ$100 million of annualised NPAT within three to four years of the August 2025 announcement, reaffirmed at FY2026 results though management explicitly disclosed the timing has been pushed out by Middle East conflict-related disruption that created 'a gap in forward booking intake unlikely to be fully recoverable' and impacted the earnings step-up expected for FY2027

Structural inbound tourism recovery in thl's core rental markets (New Zealand, Australia, Canada) — forward bookings in all three were tracking more than 20% ahead of prior year before the March 2026 Middle East conflict disrupted intake, and management reports bookings have since begun recovering (e.g. NZ intake in the last 4 weeks up ~40% versus PCP as at the August 2026 results)

North America 'one fleet' synergy project — operating the USA and Canada as a single fleet from procurement through to rentals and sales — delivered a swing to +$5.0m underlying EBIT (from +$1.5m in FY2025) despite a soft US market, with further procurement synergy realisation still to come as fleet purchases resume

Manufacturing consolidation completed: closure of the Brisbane, Australia RV manufacturing facility (December 2025) and transition of all Australasian production to Action Manufacturing in Hamilton, New Zealand; third-party manufacturing EBIT already up 55% in FY2026, with a targeted ~NZ$2.5m/annum Brisbane sublease saving still to be finalised

Fleet optimisation and moderated capital expenditure — after several years of Australasian fleet regrowth, gross fleet capex fell to $226m in FY2026 (from $287m) and is expected to stay broadly consistent in FY2027; net operating cash flow rose 67% to $67.3m (continuing operations) as a result, supporting further deleveraging

Digital transformation complete (single global Motek fleet-management platform, Microsoft Dynamics 365), with non-fleet capex normalising to $13m in FY2026 (from $42m in FY2025) after major strategic investments concluded

Two competing non-binding takeover proposals (NZ$3.10 from the BGH Capital/Trouchet consortium and NZ$3.30-3.40 from an unnamed strategic bidder), both in active due diligence as of the FY2026 results, imply third-party validation of value materially above where the stock traded through the FY2025 downturn and could crystallise value for shareholders if either converts to a binding transaction

business.description: Both the BGH Capital/Trouchet consortium ($3.10/share) and the unnamed strategic bidder ($3.30-3.40/share) approaches remain non-binding and conditional, with due diligence ongoing as of the 25 August 2026 annual results and management then expecting 'approximately a further six weeks' of due diligence (i.e. into October 2026). A Trouchet-family/SPV exclusivity and cooperation arrangement runs to 14 September 2026. There is no board recommendation, exclusivity grant to a single party, scheme of arrangement, or binding offer as at 5 September 2026 (the most recent evidence reviewed). The Board has explicitly stated 'there can be no certainty that either proposal will result in a transaction' and shareholders are 'not required to take any action'. If both approaches lapse — as the original $2.30/share approach did in 2025 — the stock could de-rate sharply from the current $2.84 back toward standalone fundamental value, which trades well below the live indicative price range

business.risk: RV sales cycle / fleet residual values
business.description: The 'Sell' segment (ex-fleet and new vehicle sales) remained in a bottom-of-cycle downturn through FY2026: ex-fleet sales volumes -25%, retail RV sales volumes -27%, sale-of-goods revenue -22% to $335.4m. 2026 has been weaker than expected for the RV sales industry generally (RV Industry Association cut its median wholesale shipment forecast 11% during the year; THOR and Camping World both cut 2026 expectations), though ex-fleet gross margins held broadly stable at 15.4%, indicating fleet depreciation/carrying values remain appropriately calibrated to realised outcomes so far

RV purchases and premium rental holidays are high-value discretionary decisions; the Middle East conflict beginning March 2026 directly disrupted booking intake and RV sales activity and, per the Chair's letter, 'impacted the significant step-up in earnings thl was expecting for FY27'

The USA rental market had a soft 2026 summer season (though strong late bookings partly offset this) and North America ROFE remains near breakeven (0.5%); management explicitly describes the USA as thl's 'largest opportunity for improvement' and says it is 'not yet where we need to be'; North American tariffs on RV chassis/components remain an ongoing cost and procurement risk

financial.risk: High capital intensity and net debt
financial.description: Net debt (excluding lease liabilities) was $435.5m at 30 June 2026, down from $492.3m a year earlier, with leverage improving to 2.32x underlying EBITDA (pre-IFRS 16) from 2.99x — but still above the original 'below $400m' year-end target the Board had set, after guidance moved as high as $460-470m mid-year on softer sales volumes, FX and working capital pressure. This demonstrates how quickly leverage can move with the sales cycle. Including IFRS 16 lease liabilities of $211.6m, total interest-bearing and lease obligations were roughly $647m against $641.1m of shareholders' equity

Revenue, earnings and debt are generated and held across at least three foreign currencies plus NZD; balance sheet items are translated at period-end cross-rates that moved materially in FY2026 (e.g. NZD:USD from 0.6068 to 0.5647), and FX was cited as a contributor to the mid-FY2026 guidance downgrade

A heavily debt-funded fleet model means net finance costs ($40.4m in FY2026) are directly sensitive to base rates across all funding jurisdictions; debt reduction is explicitly linked by management to future interest cost savings

financial.risk: Goodwill and intangible asset carrying values
financial.description: FY2025 saw material non-cash impairments of USA goodwill and USA deferred tax assets (~$40m impairment charge); FY2026 impairment charges were minimal ($0.1m), but intangible assets (including goodwill) rose to $161.6m at 30 June 2026 (from $145.5m) and remain exposed to further impairment if regional earnings (particularly North America) do not recover as guided

regulatory.risk: Cross-border tourism, immigration and visa policy
regulatory.description: Inbound tourism volumes into all of thl's rental markets are sensitive to visa policy, airline capacity allocation and government tourism-promotion settings in New Zealand, Australia and Canada, and to broader travel disruption from geopolitical shocks such as the Middle East conflict

Emissions standards, low-carbon-fleet transition requirements and freedom-camping/local-body regulation in New Zealand and Australia could raise compliance costs or constrain fleet composition and site operations over time

Any binding scheme or takeover offer would be subject to NZ Takeovers Code, competition/foreign investment approvals (e.g. NZ Overseas Investment Office, given at least one bidder consortium includes overseas private equity), and shareholder vote requirements, all of which introduce timing and completion risk even if a binding proposal emerges from the current due diligence processes. The Board has established an Independent Takeover Committee to manage these matters

macro.risk: Global travel demand cyclicality and geopolitical shocks
macro.description: International leisure travel remains below pre-COVID levels in some markets (notably the USA) and is acutely sensitive to geopolitical shocks — the March 2026 escalation of the Middle East conflict is the clearest recent example, directly disrupting international travel patterns, raising fuel prices, and creating a booking-intake gap management says 'is unlikely to be fully recoverable'

macro.severity: moderate (structural, not a downside risk per se)
macro.description: New Zealand and Australia profits are earned predominantly in the Southern Hemisphere summer (H2 of thl's fiscal year), while Canada and the USA earn profits in the Northern Hemisphere summer (H1); this means H1 and H2 results are structurally lopsided and not directly comparable, and the risk profile at any interim balance date is not representative of the full year

macro.risk: Input cost inflation (vehicle components, chassis, labour, fuel)
macro.description: Persistent inflation in vehicle build costs, tariffs on North American RV components, and the fuel-price spike associated with the Middle East conflict all pressure manufacturing margins and fleet/travel economics

macro_factors.industry_outlook: The global motorhome/campervan rental market is estimated at roughly US$1.2-2.9bn (depending on definition) in 2025/26, forecast to grow at a mid-to-high single-digit CAGR (~5-6%) through 2030-31, driven by rising interest in free-independent and experiential travel, growing airline capacity to core markets, and a younger, more diverse RV-owner demographic. International travel is broadly recovering toward, but in most markets still below, pre-pandemic levels, and remains vulnerable to geopolitical shocks (evidenced by the March 2026 Middle East conflict's impact on bookings). The RV sales sub-segment (new and used) is in its most difficult stretch in years industry-wide, with the RV Industry Association cutting its 2026 wholesale shipment forecast 11% during the year and both THOR Industries and Camping World lowering expectations; industry and thl management view this as cyclical (affordability-driven) rather than structural.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Highly cyclical in the Sell (vehicle sales) segment, which tracks consumer discretionary spending and credit conditions; moderately cyclical in Rentals, which is more resilient but still linked to international travel demand, airline capacity and consumer confidence, and can be disrupted by geopolitical shocks; Tourism attractions are the least cyclical segment and generate the group's highest returns on capital
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate-high — a capital-intensive, debt-funded fleet model means net debt levels, finance costs and dividend capacity are directly linked to base rates across NZD, AUD, USD and CAD funding markets; debt paydown is explicitly linked by management to future interest cost savings
key_input_costs: RV chassis and vehicle components (subject to North American tariffs)
Steel, aluminium and other manufacturing raw materials
Fuel/energy costs for fleet operations (spiked with the 2026 Middle East conflict)
Debt servicing costs across three-plus currencies

recent_developments.event: FY2026 annual results (Integrated Annual Report and investor presentation) released: statutory NPAT from continuing operations of $39.9m (versus a $14.1m loss in FY2025); underlying NPAT up 34% to $46.1m; underlying EBIT up 17% to $105.4m; underlying EBITDA (continuing) up 14% to $222.4m; sale-of-services (rentals) revenue up 11% to $517.5m; sale-of-goods (vehicle sales) revenue down 22% to $335.4m; net debt (ex-lease) reduced to $435.5m from $492.3m, leverage improved to 2.32x from 2.99x; closing rental fleet up 10% to 8,587 vehicles; full-year dividend up 62% to 10.5 cents per share (final 7.5cps, 100% imputed/10% franked); net operating cash flow up 67% to $67.3m; total group revenue (including discontinued UK/Ireland operations) of $885.3m; shareholders' equity $641.1m; lease liabilities $211.6m; cash $46.4m; ROFE improved to 8.7% from 7.6% but remains below the 15% target. Management confirmed both non-binding takeover approaches remain live, in due diligence, with 'approximately a further six weeks' expected as at the results date, and reaffirmed the NZ$100m underlying NPAT Growth Roadmap goal while explicitly disclosing its timing has shifted due to Middle East conflict disruption to bookings and RV sales

A competing, non-binding indicative offer emerged from an unnamed party the Board considers a 'credible strategic acquirer' at NZ$3.30-3.40 per share (valuing thl at up to ~$752m), superior to the BGH Capital consortium's revised NZ$3.10/share proposal; the Board granted due diligence access to both parties under confidentiality agreements. Separately, the Trouchet family shareholders (holding ~11.8-19.9% depending on measurement) extended their exclusivity/cooperation agreement with the BGH-led SPV, initially to 14 September 2026 and (per later reporting) with the broader lock-up cooperation term pushed out to 31 March 2027

BGH Capital/Trouchet family consortium tabled a revised, non-binding indicative offer of NZ$3.10 per share (up from the original NZ$2.30/share approach first received June 2025), on condition the Board grant due diligence access; the Board did so, and confirmed it expects any binding proposal following due diligence to reflect a price at or above $3.10/share. THL simultaneously cut FY2026 underlying NPAT guidance to $40-43m (from $43-47m) and raised expected year-end net debt guidance to $460-470m (from below $400m), citing softer vehicle sales volumes (notably from early March 2026), Middle East conflict impacts on sales, softer Australian domestic rental conditions and FX headwinds; Forsyth Barr downgraded THL to Neutral (from Outperform) with a $3.10 price target, and Ord Minnett also downgraded to Hold

Trading update: THL guided underlying NPAT from continuing operations of approximately $46m for FY2026, a significant step-up from the $40-43m May guidance and close to the top of the original $43-47m range, alongside net debt around $436m — subsequently confirmed (at $46.1m / $435.5m) in the August annual results

Completed the divestment of the UK & Ireland Rentals & Sales business to Indie Campers for approximately $57m of proceeds including ~$8m of goodwill/gain, following a conditional agreement announced in H1 FY2026 (originally reported at ~$58.3m); the business is now presented as a discontinued operation under NZ IFRS 5, with FY2025 comparatives restated to exclude it

Completed closure of the Brisbane, Australia RV manufacturing facility and transitioned all Australasian production to Action Manufacturing in Hamilton, New Zealand; also closed/exited two loss-making Australian retail dealerships (Sydney RV and Kratzmann) and rationalised the product range

Board rejected an unsolicited, non-binding $2.30/share conditional indication of interest from the BGH Capital/Trouchet family consortium (first received June 2025), stating the offer significantly undervalued the company and that the Board's view of value was 'well north of $3.00 per share'; the Board also released its Growth Roadmap targeting >$100m annualised NPAT within three to four years

takeover_status.summary: CONFIRMED as at 25 August 2026 (FY2026 annual results, the most recent primary-source disclosure) and no subsequent binding development found in web searches through 5 September 2026: two non-binding, conditional indicative proposals remain before the Board — a revised $3.10/share all-cash proposal from the BGH Capital/Trouchet family consortium, and a competing $3.30-3.40/share proposal from an unnamed party the Board describes as 'a credible strategic acquirer'. Both are in active due diligence, with 'management sessions and site visits' having 'recently commenced' as at 25 August 2026, and the Board 'currently expects the due diligence phase to continue for approximately a further six weeks' from that date (i.e. into approximately early-to-mid October 2026). No board recommendation, scheme of arrangement, binding offer, exclusivity grant to a single bidder, or withdrawal/lapse of either approach has been announced as at 5 September 2026. A separate exclusivity/cooperation agreement between the Trouchet family shareholders and the BGH-led SPV (restricting the Trouchet stake, ~11.8-19.9% depending on the measurement date) was extended and, per the most recent reporting found, runs with milestones to 14 September 2026 and a broader cooperation term to 31 March 2027 — this is a lock-up on the Trouchet shares' saleability, not a transaction deadline, but its 14 September date sits just after this analysis and is a near-term point to watch. Both the Board's own public statements and Forsyth Barr's research (Neutral, $3.10 target, no updated public target found post-August-2026) treat completion as uncertain rather than assured; no analyst source reviewed provides a numeric probability estimate more recent than the ~June 2026 commentary. The stock closed FY2026 (30 June 2026) at $2.90 and recent web sources place it around $2.75-$2.87 in August 2026, versus the live indicative range of $3.10-$3.40 and a 52-week high near $2.98 — consistent with the market pricing a meaningful but well short of full/certain probability of deal completion at or near the upper end of the range. INVESTORS SHOULD VERIFY CURRENT STATUS DIRECTLY VIA NZX/ASX ANNOUNCEMENTS before relying on this for time-sensitive decisions, given the due diligence timeline points to a likely news event in the September-October 2026 window.

items.vs_prior: moderated / lowered vs the prior two years of rapid Australasian fleet regrowth
items.notes: Reflects substantial completion of the Australasian fleet regrowth programme (Group closing fleet +10% to 8,587 in FY2026) and a focus on hire-day growth, RevPARV and utilisation over further fleet expansion; North America fleet capex 'significantly reduced' to manage through the cycle, which will increase average fleet age

guidance.management_commentary: Chair Cathy Quinn and CEO Grant Webster framed FY2026 as a year of 'meaningful action and progress', delivering a profit rebound (underlying NPAT +34% to $46.1m) and completing all four Growth Roadmap strategic initiatives announced in August 2025 (UK & Ireland divestment, Australasian manufacturing consolidation, Australian retail sales rationalisation, and North American 'one fleet' synergies), while explicitly disclosing that the Middle East conflict beginning March 2026 created a booking-intake gap 'unlikely to be fully recoverable' that has pushed out the timing of both the FY2027 earnings step-up and the longer-dated $100m NPAT goal. Management continues to describe rentals as 'the engine' of the business, states the USA 'remains our largest opportunity for improvement' where the company is 'not yet where we need to be', and expects continued rental revenue growth into FY2027 alongside disciplined cost and balance sheet management. On the takeover approaches, the Board (via its Independent Takeover Committee) confirmed at the FY2026 results that both the BGH Capital/Trouchet consortium ($3.10/share) and the unnamed strategic bidder ($3.30-3.40/share) remain in active due diligence, with management sessions and site visits recently commenced and roughly six further weeks of due diligence expected from 25 August 2026; both proposals remain non-binding, conditional, and subject to a range of conditions, with the Board stating there is no certainty either will result in a transaction and shareholders are not required to take any action at this time.

bull_case: Two competing non-binding takeover proposals (NZ$3.10 and NZ$3.30-3.40 per share), both now in active due diligence with management sessions and site visits underway as of the FY2026 results, sit well above the Board's own August 2025 stated view of intrinsic value ('well north of $3.00') and above where the stock traded through the FY2025 downturn — a credible valuation floor and a potential near-term catalyst if either converts into a binding, premium-paying transaction, with a decision point plausible in the September-October 2026 window based on management's stated due diligence timeline

FY2026 marked a clear earnings inflection on a continuing-operations basis: underlying NPAT up 34% to $46.1m, underlying EBIT up 17% and underlying EBITDA up 14%, net debt down from $492m to $436m with leverage improved to 2.32x from 2.99x, operating cash flow up 67% to $67.3m, and the full-year dividend raised 62% to 10.5cps — tangible evidence the Growth Roadmap initiatives (manufacturing consolidation, Australian retail rationalisation completed, North American synergies, UK & Ireland exit completed) are delivering, even before the RV sales cycle turns

Rentals — the highest-margin, most resilient segment and management's stated 'engine' of the business — grew sale-of-services revenue 11% in FY2026 to $517.5m on an 11.5% larger average fleet, with New Zealand (+17% revenue, 13.3% ROFE) and Canada (on track for a record 2026 summer season) demonstrating the strongest underlying momentum, and recent booking-intake data suggesting demand deferred by the Middle East conflict is starting to be recovered rather than permanently lost

A genuine, if partial, vertical-integration moat (build via a now-fully-consolidated Action Manufacturing in Hamilton, rent via a multi-tier global brand portfolio, sell via owned dealerships) differentiates thl from rental-only or sales-only competitors in a fragmented global market, and third-party manufacturing EBIT already up 55% in FY2026 evidences early payoff from the Brisbane-to-Hamilton consolidation

The RV sales downturn — the single largest drag on group earnings since FY2024 — is viewed by both industry participants and management as cyclical (affordability-driven) rather than structural, with stable ex-fleet sales margins (15.4%) indicating fleet carrying values remain well calibrated; a cyclical recovery in RV sales markets is one of the four drivers management still cites as intact for the $100m NPAT goal, offering meaningful earnings torque on top of an already-improving rental base
bear_case: The core investment case now hinges heavily on an unresolved, twice-extended takeover process: both approaches remain non-binding, conditional and subject to due diligence, financing and Takeovers Code/regulatory approval, with no board recommendation as at 5 September 2026 and management's own August 2026 disclosure stating due diligence would run a further ~6 weeks — shareholders who buy for takeover premium risk being left holding a standalone stock (last priced well below the live $3.10-3.40 indicative range) if both proposals lapse, as the original $2.30/share BGH approach did in 2025

Guidance volatility in calendar 2026 (FY26 underlying NPAT cut from $43-47m to $40-43m in May/June, then raised back to ~$46m in July) and a similar round-trip in net debt guidance ($400m target blown out to $460-470m before recovering to $435.5m) illustrate how quickly and unpredictably results can move with the RV sales cycle, FX, geopolitical shocks and working capital — a business that is difficult to forecast with confidence even for management, and one where an external shock (the Middle East conflict) has already pushed out the FY2027 earnings step-up management had been promising

Return on Funds Employed remains well below the company's own 15% through-the-cycle target (8.7% in FY2026, up only modestly from 7.6%), with North America still near breakeven (0.5% ROFE) and Australia at 6.8%; the $100m NPAT Growth Roadmap goal has already had its timeline pushed out once, and management itself frames FY2026 progress as real but incomplete ('there is more work to do', 'not yet where we need to be' on the USA)

US market weakness is only partly cyclical: North America ROFE remains near zero, industry-wide RV sales forecasts (RVIA, THOR, Camping World) were cut further during FY2026, and the March 2026 Middle East conflict created a booking gap management says is 'unlikely to be fully recoverable' — a reminder that thl's globally diversified footprint is also globally exposed to geopolitical shocks outside its control

Even after FY2026 deleveraging, thl carries substantial net debt ($435.5m ex-lease, plus $211.6m of lease liabilities) against a capital-intensive, cyclical fleet business exposed to at least three foreign currencies and interest-rate movements in each; a renewed downturn in RV sales, inbound tourism or consumer confidence would quickly pressure both leverage and the still-fragile earnings recovery, and continued dividend growth is explicitly conditioned on that recovery persisting
